Theme

School & learning

exam noun

also examination, test, school test, quiz, take an exam, pass an exam, examine, flunk a test, fail a test, pass a test, flunk an exam, tough exam

classical

Cic. Off. 1.144: in athlētārum probātiōne
Traupman 26, 27, 32
M-O s.v. test, quiz
Traupman 29: cadere in probātiōne, to flunk a test
Traupman 30: probātiōnem sustinēre, to pass a test
Traupman 311

probātiō, probātiōnis f.

noun, third declension

a test, an examination

Classically a trial or inspection, of athletes or recruits; Traupman’s word for a test. To pass a test is probātiōnem sustinēre, to fail it in probātiōne cadere (Traupman 29, 30; see fail); to study for one, ad probātiōnem sē parāre (Morgan–Owens).

Other words

  • exāmen, exāminis n. — an exam

    noun, third declension · also used · modern · M-O s.v. test: exam, examination, after Grosse (1846) and Egger; Traupman 311

    Classically a swarm of bees, then the tongue of a balance, and so a weighing (Pers. 1.6; Ov. Met. 9.552, Lewis & Short). To take an exam is exāmen subīre, to pass it exāmen superāre (Morgan–Owens).

  • perīculum, perīculī n. — a trial, a test

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Ter. Eun. 476: fac perīclum in litterīs; M-O s.v. test, quiz

    With facere, to put to the test; its everyday sense is danger.

  • experīmentum, experīmentī n. — a trial, a test

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Levi–Bini p. 271: experīmentum Latīnī sermōnis, an exam in Latin; M-O s.v. test, quiz

    A proof or trial, mostly after Augustus (Quint. 2.5.15, Lewis & Short); Levi and Bini’s word for a school exam.

  • exāminō, exāmināre, exāmināvī, exāminātum — examine, test

    verb, first conjugation · also used · modern · Traupman 29; Traupman 311

    Classically “to weigh”, of scales and of thought (Cic. Tusc. 1.43, Lewis & Short); of testing pupils it is modern.

  • quaestiuncula, quaestiunculae f. — a little question; a quiz

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. de Or. 1.102: quaestiunculam alicui pōnere (Lewis & Short); Traupman 31, for “quiz”

  • probātiuncula, probātiunculae f. — quiz, short test

    noun, first declension · also used · modern · Traupman 367

  • Fac perīclum in litterīs, fac in palaestrā, in mūsicīs.

    Test him in letters, test him at wrestling, in music.Ter. Eun. 476–477

    Get ready for tomorrow’s test.composed
